newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to extend high toy tariffs for three years.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to extend high toy tariffs for three years.

text.p: The Brazilian government has decided to extend high tariffs on toy imports for another three years because the domestic toy industry has still not adjusted to overseas competition, a senior trade official said.

Helio Mauro Franca, director of foreign trade policy in the Ministry of Industry and Commerce, told Reuters that Brazil had informed the World Trade Organization and was holding consultations this week with internationnal trade partners.

"The decision will only become official with the publication in the Official Journal of a decree. But we have informed the WTO of our intention to extend the tariffs...and are now consulting with our trade partners," he said.
In July, Brazil hiked to 70 percent from 20 percent tariffs on imported toys, provoking angry reactions from U.S. toy manufacturers and the European Union.
Franca said tariffs would be 63 percent in 1997, the maximum possible under WTO rules, 49 percent in 1998 and 35 percent in 1999, with the safeguards expiring at the end of that year.
When Industry and Commerce Minister Francisco Dornelles announced the higher tariff in July, he said the measure would expire at the end of 1996.
Dornelles said that the Brazilian toy industry would have until then to "get its house in order" and modernize.
But Franca said six months had proved too little time for Brazilian firms to prepare themselves for competition against cheaper imports.
"These six months were not sufficient to make good the damage done to the domestic industry and give them time to adjust (to competition)," he said.
Franca said the government expected to complete consultations in Geneva with interested parties this week.
He said Brasilia expected to publish a decree in the final days of December, so that a provisional measure introducing the 63 percent tariff for 1997 can come into effect on January 1.
